title: Chess reading library
scope: 25 curated titles from the existing local library. This is a starter selection, not a complete list of chess PDFs on Internet Archive.
selection_note: Reading levels and recommendations are editorial judgments based on sampled contents and lessons. Historical references are marked separately from the suggested learning path.
verification_note: All 25 local PDFs were opened and sampled visually. Edition notes use title pages and front matter. This is not a page-by-page completeness review. Ten Archive item pages listed PDFs; fifteen online checks were inconclusive. Download URLs come from the existing download records, not a fresh download test.
page_numbers: One-based PDF page numbers for the linked local files, not printed page numbers. Paths are relative to the project root.
notation_guide: English descriptive notation names squares relative to the player, such as K-B3. Modern algebraic notation uses fixed squares, such as Nf3. Converting old game scores requires the full position and side to move.

reading_paths.title: Build an understanding of the game
reading_paths.method: Read one short lesson, reproduce its position on a board, and look for the idea in one of your own games.

reading_paths.title: Know what to do after the opening
reading_paths.method: Describe the position, choose two candidate plans, and explain the opponent's strongest response.

reading_paths.title: Finish the game with a plan
reading_paths.method: Begin with basic mates, then opposition and pawn endings. Verify study solutions before memorizing them.

reading_paths.title: See ideas in complete games
reading_paths.method: Choose one game, predict critical moves, and compare your reason with the annotation.

books.title: Chess Fundamentals
books.author: José Raúl Capablanca
books.why_read: A compact way to connect simple endings to the rest of the game. Start here if you know the rules but struggle to explain why a move helps.

edition.description: Harcourt, Brace scan; copyright 1921; printing date not established
edition.note: The filename gives the work's 1921 date, not a verified date for this printing.

start_here.section: Some Simple Mates
start_here.exercise: Play the rook-and-king mate against a defending king. Explain which squares each move removes before moving.

books.reading_note: Uses descriptive notation. Treat opening analysis as historical and check concrete lines on a board.

pdf.scan_note: Clear text and diagram in the sampled lesson; yellowed pages.

books.title: Common Sense in Chess
books.author: Emanuel Lasker
books.suggested_level: Beginner with the rules learned to intermediate
books.why_read: Short lectures make a useful companion to game reviews: the emphasis is on the purpose behind development and practical decisions.

edition.description: 1896 English edition, Bellairs & Co.
edition.note: The local title page confirms 1896. This is a different scan from the 1910 Archive copy that reports missing pages 15-18.

start_here.section: Lecture No. 1
start_here.exercise: After each opening example, name the development gain or loss and the concrete reply that makes it matter.

books.reading_note: The prose is old-fashioned and the principles need positional exceptions. Uses descriptive notation.

pdf.scan_note: The sampled pages are readable but faint; enlargement helps.

books.title: Chess Strategy
books.author: Edward Lasker
books.why_read: Connects opening development to pawn structure and later plans. Useful when a player knows opening moves but loses direction once those moves run out.

edition.description: Second revised edition, translated by J. du Mont; later reprint
edition.note: The copyright/history page lists reprints through 1931. Archive labels the item 1917; the filename's 1915 date is the first-publication date.

start_here.section: Contents: General Principles and The Opening
start_here.exercise: Choose one example from The Opening and describe how the pawn structure changes the best squares for the pieces.

books.reading_note: Descriptive notation and historical opening analysis; prioritize the explanations over memorizing variations.

pdf.local_path: books/Edward Lasker - Chess Strategy (1915).pdf
pdf.scan_note: Readable contents and title pages; the text layer sometimes misreads chess notation.

access.archive_pdf: Listed on the checked item page

books.title: The Principles of Chess in Theory and Practice
books.author: James Mason
books.why_read: Useful for moving from isolated rules to coordinated plans. Its discussion of planning is a good prompt for explaining what several pieces are trying to achieve together.

edition.description: 1894 London edition, Horace Cox
edition.note: Year confirmed on the local title page.

start_here.section: General Principles: Plan
start_here.exercise: Before reading a continuation, write a plan and the opponent's strongest objection to it.

books.reading_note: Victorian prose and descriptive notation make this a slower read than the first three foundation books.

pdf.local_path: books/James Mason - The Principles of Chess in Theory and Practice (1894).pdf
pdf.scan_note: The sampled text is clear but densely set.

books.title: The Art of Chess
books.author: James Mason
books.why_read: Starts from endings and builds toward more complex positions. The opposition section is a useful focused assignment for a player who misjudges king-and-pawn endings.

edition.description: Fourth edition, revised and enlarged; revisions by Leopold Hoffer
edition.note: The local preface and Archive record identify the 1913 revision; the filename's 1895 date is not this edition.

start_here.section: Book I: Endings - Notes on the Opposition
start_here.exercise: Set up the opposition diagrams and change the side to move. Explain why that changes the result or the route.

books.reading_note: Uses descriptive notation; confirm specific old endgame analyses before turning them into exercises.

pdf.scan_note: Readable text and opposition diagrams in the sample.

books.title: My Chess Career
books.author: José Raúl Capablanca
books.why_read: Pairs a player's own account of improvement with selected games. Useful for studying how an advantage becomes a concrete plan.

edition.description: Dover edition with introduction and afterword by Irving Chernev
edition.note: The local copyright page identifies the 1966 edition with new material, not the 1920 original named in the filename.

start_here.section: Contents: The Match with Marshall
start_here.exercise: Choose one Marshall-match game. Pause at each exchange and predict which side benefits from the remaining pieces.

books.reading_note: The PDF page number differs substantially from the printed page number. Uses descriptive notation.

books.title: Morphy's Games of Chess
books.author: Philip W. Sergeant
books.why_read: A rewarding place to see why a lead in development matters. Use selected games to connect open lines, active pieces and an exposed king.

edition.description: 1916 edition, G. Bell and Sons
edition.note: Title and year confirmed on the local title page; this is Sergeant's collection, not the separate Lowenthal volume.

start_here.section: Part I, Section I: American Chess Congress Games
start_here.exercise: In one game, mark the moment when development becomes a concrete threat. Check the defender's alternatives before praising a sacrifice.

books.reading_note: Some sections contain odds, consultation or blindfold games. Keep those contexts distinct from ordinary tournament games.

books.title: The Middle Game in Chess
books.author: Eugene Znosko-Borovsky
books.why_read: Addresses the common question of what to do after the opening. Its framework connects a position's advantages and weaknesses to a plan.

edition.description: 1930 reprint, G. Bell and Sons
edition.note: The title and publication-history pages identify 1930; the work was first published in 1922.

start_here.section: Construction and Execution of the Plan
start_here.exercise: Describe one position in terms of material, time and space, then choose a plan and an opponent reply that could challenge it.

books.reading_note: A planning framework is a guide, not a substitute for calculation. Uses descriptive notation.

pdf.scan_note: Clear sampled lesson text on yellowed pages.

books.title: Lasker's Manual of Chess
books.author: Emanuel Lasker
books.why_read: A broad reference for relating combinations to positional judgment. Best approached by selected sections rather than as the first book a beginner reads.

edition.description: English edition with a 1947 McKay copyright notice and Reinfeld appreciation
edition.note: The scan contains later editorial material; its printing date is not established by the filename's 1925 date.

start_here.section: Contents: The Combination and Position Play
start_here.exercise: Choose one combination and identify the positional feature that makes it possible before calculating the line.

books.reading_note: Dense prose and descriptive notation. Do not treat this scan as the original German edition.

books.title: My System
books.author: Aron Nimzowitsch
books.why_read: Gives a vocabulary for explaining positional moves: files, pawn chains, blockade and restraint. Useful for turning a quiet move into an understandable plan.

edition.description: 21st Century Edition, edited by Lou Hays, introduction by Yasser Seirawan
edition.note: The local file is a modern English adaptation in algebraic notation, not the 1925 original. Exact edition year was not found in the inspected front matter.

start_here.section: Chapter 2: On Open Files
start_here.exercise: Find the intended entry square before moving a rook to an open file. Ask what would prevent the rook from reaching it.

books.reading_note: Treat its concepts as questions to test in a position, not rules that override tactics.

books.title: Chess Studies; or, Endings of Games
books.author: Kling & Horwitz
books.why_read: A collection of compact ending positions that rewards precise calculation. Useful for practicing the difference between a plausible move and the only move that holds or wins.

edition.description: 1851 edition, edited by Henry C. Mott
edition.note: Title page confirms the edition; front matter includes an errata notice.

start_here.section: King and Pawns Against King and Pawns: Study No. I
start_here.exercise: Solve the first position on a board, then test the losing alternatives and explain why they fail.

books.reading_note: Check errata and verify old study solutions before using them as graded puzzles.

books.title: A Collection of Two Hundred Chess Problems
books.author: Francis Healey
books.why_read: Useful for exploring surprising quiet moves and carefully arranged mating ideas. This is a problem-composition collection, so it complements practical tactics rather than replacing them.

edition.description: 1866 London edition, Longmans, Green and Co.
edition.note: The local title page says 1866, correcting the filename and older manifest's 1862 label.

start_here.section: Frontispiece problem: The Charm
start_here.exercise: Try the frontispiece's mate-in-five challenge without moving pieces, then verify every defense on a board.

books.reading_note: Composed problems can differ sharply from practical game positions. Solutions and piece placements need manual verification.

books.title: The International Chess Congress, St. Petersburg 1909
books.author: Emanuel Lasker
books.why_read: A strong fit for studying how an annotator explains both merit and weakness in a move. Use one game at a time and compare your reasoning with the notes.

edition.description: 1910 English edition; tournament held in 1909

start_here.section: Preface: how to use the annotations
start_here.exercise: Choose a tournament game, hide the notes and write your own explanation of a critical move before comparing.

books.reading_note: Uses descriptive notation. Historical annotations should be checked before being treated as engine conclusions.

books.title: The Modern Chess Instructor
books.author: Wilhelm Steinitz
books.why_read: Useful for examining the reasoning behind positional principles and comparing them with concrete play. Read the principles as arguments to test, then study an illustrative game.

edition.description: 1889, Part I, G. P. Putnam's Sons
edition.note: The local title page explicitly identifies Part I; this entry does not claim to contain every volume.

start_here.section: The Modern School and the Principles of Play: continuation
start_here.exercise: Select one claim about king activity or defense and find the conditions under which it would or would not apply.

books.reading_note: The opening variations are historical. Do not present the author's general claims as universal rules.
